title: Systemic Evidence Hierarchy Reversal by ANAC — Tertiary Corporate Evidence Preferred Over Primary Official Investigation (PDI CCTV Exoneration)

confidence.note: ANAC's dismissal explicitly preferred LATAM's corporate statements over the PDI's CCTV exoneration. Case update rates this as HIGH strength, cross‑referenced with BR‑013 and BR‑014.

allegation_summary: In dismissing the passenger’s complaint, ANAC committed a systemic evidence hierarchy reversal by prioritising LATAM’s self‑serving internal corporate statements over the primary, official investigation by the Chilean PDI. The PDI reviewed airport CCTV footage and formally exonerated the passenger, determining he committed no offense. This conclusive evidence from a competent law enforcement authority was available but wholly disregarded. Instead, ANAC relied on tertiary evidence — LATAM’s internal position — to dismiss the complaint. This perversion of evidentiary standards violates the CDC’s mandate to facilitate the consumer’s defence (Art. 6, VIII) and the principle of official truth‑seeking in administrative proceedings (Lei 9.784/99, Art. 29). It also contradicts the objectives of the National Consumer Policy (CDC Art. 4) by failing to protect the consumer’s interests and by creating an imbalance that favours the supplier.
